A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TAPTRv3. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support matching content across the substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original tracking evaluations, component ablations, memory-size experiments, and qualitative tracking results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 reports original tracking evaluations and ablations, alongside additional runtime, GPU-memory, and backbone/resolution comparisons.

M1.justification: The default backbone changes from ResNet-50 to ResNet-18 (Section 4.2). The four-layer decoder, CCA, VLTA, losses, and scene-cut-triggered global matching retain their core procedures. This is a limited architecture revision for efficiency.

E1.justification: Both versions train on the same 11,000-video Kubric dataset and evaluate tracking on Kinetics, RGB-Stacking, RoboTAP, and DAVIS. DAVIS moves to the appendix, and the Kinetics scene-cut subset already exists in v1. Additional resource analyses do not establish a new tracking domain or task.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 1 and 13 add Track-On, Anthro-LocoTrack, and BootsTAPNext-B to the existing tracking comparisons, retaining the earlier comparators. Table 11 additionally compares runtime against CoTracker and TAPTRv2. These extend the comparison set without replacing its basic scope.

E3.justification: The main model configuration changes to ResNet-18 with 384×512 training images, versus ResNet-50 and 512×512 in v1. The reported ablation budget changes from 28,000 to 33,000 iterations. New runtime evaluation specifies 384×512 inputs and eight-frame windows with stride four, alongside expanded memory-size settings. Accuracy evaluation retains first-query mode and 256×256 inputs.

E4.justification: v2 adds a RoboTAP memory sweep from 8 to 1,024 frames, runtime and GPU-memory analyses, and a joint backbone/training-resolution comparison (Figure 4 and Tables 11–12). These substantially extend investigation of practical efficiency. Existing component ablations and qualitative examples remain; the scene-cut subset analysis moves from v1 Table 6 to v2 Table 10.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix A.2 newly reports five repetitions and averaging for the runtime experiments. Neither version reports tracking seed counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The new repetition statement concerns timing, not additional tracking-training runs.

E6.justification: v2 Table 12 preserves v1's main results and adds the lighter configuration: Kinetics/RGB-Stacking/RoboTAP/DAVIS AJ changes from 54.5/73.0/64.6/63.2 to 54.9/72.3/64.5/63.2 under different training/model conditions. Numerous ablation values change, new baseline and resource results appear, and Table 2 removes localization and occlusion scores. These are extensive reporting changes, not uniform same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–9 retain the same substance. Neither version adds or removes formal theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the three central contributions: spatial context through CCA, temporal context through VLTA, and scene-cut-triggered global matching for robust long-video tracking. Sharper abstract wording does not materially redefine these contributions; the introduction and conclusion retain the same overall performance and competitiveness claims.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies the benefits of unrestricted temporal context by discussing memory exhaustion and bounded-memory operation. It adds explanations for improved efficiency and a dedicated limitations section describing restricted frame parallelism and the speed/accuracy tradeoff of larger windows. These add practical applicability boundaries without overturning the tracking interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses approximately 33,000 main training iterations, clarifies equal context-grid intervals across feature scales, and documents FIFO memory management with a 512-frame streaming budget. It also supplies runtime measurement details and explicit supplementary-video filenames. Most existing implementation information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of TAG, AnthroTAP, Track-On, and TAPNext, and credits Context-PIPs in the spatial-context motivation. These update the relationship to recent tracking research while retaining the basic positioning around DETR-style tracking and contextual attention.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites of the abstract, introduction, explanations, and conclusion, plus renamed global-matching terminology. The appendix gains clearer subdivisions, and DAVIS discussion moves there. Most technical prose and the main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation. v1 Figures 1–2 are removed, a new memory-sweep chart appears, and retained diagrams and qualitative figures are resized and renumbered. Benchmark and scene-cut tables are split between main text and appendix, new efficiency tables appear, and Table 2 loses two metric columns.

improvement.justification: The added efficiency measurements, memory analysis, recent comparators, and explicit limitations make practical performance easier to assess. Table 12 transparently preserves the earlier configuration and documents the lighter model's accuracy tradeoffs. The gains are moderate: core scientific support remains similar, Table 2 loses localization and occlusion results, and the windowed runtime protocol limits conclusions about default streaming speed.
